questions.question:
**Select the sentence that best expresses the sentence that is in indirect speech below.**

I urged my brother not to argue with his wife.

options.text: I said to my brother, “Please don’t argue with your wife”.
I told to my brother, “Don’t you dare to argue with your wife”.
I warned my brother, “Don’t argue with your wife”.
I told my brother, “Why are you arguing with your wife?”

questions.solution: The word ‘**urge’** means to try to earnestly persuade someone to do something. Therefore, out of all the given sentences, the one that best captures this meaning is **option 1 **since the quoted sentence starts with ‘**please’**.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

The games ______ are cricket and hockey.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**he likes to watch**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given question, the phrase that fills the blank must function as a **dependent clause**. In fact, even without the clause, the remaining sentence is grammatically correct and meaningful.
 
• Therefore, the dependent clause in the blank must add some additional information and acts as an ‘**adjective clause**’. Like an adjective, this clause describes a noun – i.e. ‘games’.
 
• Here is the full correct sentence: *The games he likes to watch are cricket and hockey.*

Hence, option 2 is the correct option.

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• Keep in mind that a dependent clause is never a complete, independent sentence. Therefore, **option 3** is incorrect.
 
• Also, **option 1** is incorrect since it uses ‘whom’ which is used to refer to people, not things.
 
• **Option 4** is a grammatically incorrect construction.

questions.question:
**Given below is a sentence with a blank. Select the correct segment that completes the sentence. **

The newspaper article describes how our ideas about table manners _________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**have changed over the decades**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The given context of the blank clearly needs a verb form that indicates a sense of an action that has taken place once or many times before now, specifically experiences or changes.
 
• This is best represented by the usage of present perfect tense as seen in options 2 and 4.
 
• For eg.:

 *Mankind **has evolved** so quickly over the last 100 years.*
 
• In the given context, since, ‘table manners’ is plural, the verb form that follows must agree with it. It will therefore, be ‘**have changed’**, not ‘has changed’.
 
• Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Given below is a sentence with a blank. Select the correct segment that completes the sentence.**

She knew the medicine would taste terrible, but _________ she had to take it.
questions.solution:
The construction **‘*in order* + infinitive form of verb’** is used to express the purpose of something.

For eg: *In order to teach Sumit a lesson about cleanliness, his mother made him clean the bedrooms of everyone in the family.*

Therefore, in the given context, option 1 makes perfect use of this construction and fits meaningfully in the blank.

The correct sentence is:

*She knew the medicine would taste terrible, but **in order to get well** she had to take it.*

None of the other options express this meaning. Hence, **option 1 is correct.**

questions.question: In the context of the given passage, what is the most appropriate word for Blank 1?
questions.solution:
In the given context, we can see the phrase ‘experimenting with’ and deduce that the subject must be dealing with the subject of fingerprints in a more **casual manner** than a ‘job’ or a ‘duty’.

Out of the remaining options, the word ‘hobby’ fits the blank better since it suggests a degree of passion towards the specific activity or subject. ‘Pastime’, on the other hand, indicates that someone merely does something to pass their spare time away.

Hence, **option 4, *hobby*, is correct.**

questions.question: In the context of the given passage, what is the most appropriate word for Blank 2?
questions.solution:
The word ‘**fact’** is used to refer to something that is known or proved to be true. In the context of the passage, this refers to the knowledge that no two fingerprints are the same, which has been proved to be true.

The other options are incorrect here since they refer to ‘a topic under discussion or up for debate’ as opposed to actual truthful information.

Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question: In the context of the given passage, what is the most appropriate word for Blank 3?
questions.solution:
If you **serve** something such as **a prison sentence** or an apprenticeship, you spend a period of time doing it.

We can see that it fits the context of the passage perfectly in a way that none of the other options do.

Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.**

A person who draws maps
questions.solution:
A **cartographer** is defined as a person who draws or produces maps. Hence, **option 4** is correct.

Here are the meanings of the other words:

questions.question:
**The passage consists of six sentences. The first and sixth sentences (S1 and S6) are given. The middle four sentences (P, Q, R, S) are given in jumbled order. Find out the proper order for the four sentences.**

S1: Most people who have come close to death say they remember nothing.

P. It may permanently change a person’s perceptions of what is real and important

Q. The near-death experience is among the most powerful experiences that a person can have.

R. That ‘something’ might be a near-death experience.

S. However, a third or more may later report that ‘something happened.’

S6: However, one extraordinary aspect of near-death experience is that a person’s culture, religion, race or education does not affect the pattern of the experience.
questions.solution:
The first sentence to follow sentence 1 should logically be **Q.** This is because it is the only one that **elaborates on the topic introduced in sentence 1** before the other sentences start getting into further details.

The next logical sentence should be **P**. This is because the **pronoun ‘it’ **in the sentence **clearly refers to the subject of ‘near-death experience’** first brought up in Q.

After this, the next sentence will be **S **since it starts with the word ‘**however’** and goes on to offer information **that directly contrasts the point brought up by P** ie*. *that ‘*it may permanently change a person’s perceptions of what is real and important’.*

Finally, the **last sentence will be R,** which defines the ‘something’ mentioned in S.

Hence, the correct order of sentences is **QPSR** and the correct answer is **option 2.**

questions.question:
**Select the sentence that best expresses the passive form of the sentence given below.**

I remember my sister taking me to a beautiful monastery in Ladakh.

options.text: I remember me being taken to a beautiful monastery in Ladakh.
I remember being taken to a beautiful monastery in Ladakh by my sister.
I remember I being taken to a beautiful monastery in Ladakh by my sister.
I remember that I was taken to a beautiful monastery in Ladakh by my sister.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I remember being taken to a beautiful monastery in Ladakh by my sister.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

While converting a sentence to passive voice:

 
• The Object of the Active voice becomes the Subject of the Passive voice and vice versa.
 
• In the given sentence, it contains a gerund​
 
• The following syntax should be followed while converting into passive for sentences containing **gerund:**
 
• **A gerund** is an -ing form. It can be simple or perfect, active or passive:

 
 

 
 Active
 Passive
 
 

 **Simple gerund**
 writing
 being written
 
 

 **Perfect gerund**
 having written
 having been written

 
 
 

 

 
• 
 Gerunds are used after prepositions and verbs normally followed by a gerund.
 
 
• 
 Since the sentence given is the simple gerund (Vᵢₙg), its passive should be (being + V₃)
 
 
• 
 '**I**' becomes the subject (subjective pronoun for **'me') **and '**my sister**' becomes the object in passive.
 

**The passive voice of the given sentence will be:** *I remember being taken to a beautiful monastery in Ladakh by my sister.*

questions.question:
**The sentence below has three segments. One of the segments may contain an error. Indicate that part. In case no part has error, select the option ‘No error’.**

I have been travelling by bus (1)/ since several years (2) / but have never come across such a reckless driver (3)/ No error (4)

options.text: But have never come across such a reckless driver
I have been travelling by bus

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is __**Since several years**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **'for several years' **should be there in place of **'since several years'**
 
• The present perfect continuous tense shows that something started in the past and is continuing at the present time. 
 
• We use 'for' with a period of time in the past, present or future.
 
• 'For' refers to periods of time, i.e. 3 years, 4 hours, ages, a long time, months, years.
 
 
• Eg. I have been walking for five hours.
 
 
 
• 'Since' is used to present the starting point of an action that continues in the present and takes the usage of the present perfect or present perfect continuous tense verb. We use 'since' with a point in time in the past
 
 
• Eg. I have been walking since 10 p.m.* *
 
 
 
• *​*According to the usage and examples that are given above, '**since**' is used instead of 'for'.

**The correct sentence is: ***I have been travelling by bus **for** several years but have never come across such a reckless driver.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.**

PERNICIOUS
questions.solution:
The word ‘**pernicious’** means ‘having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way’.

Out of the given options, we can see that the word closest in meaning to this word is ‘**spiteful’** which means ‘wanting to upset or hurt someone’.

Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

The Indian Railways are setting to run special trains for the Ardh Kumbh Mela-the mega holy event that is slated to start soon.
questions.solution:
The construction **‘set to + do something**’ is used to suggest that something is planned or ready to get started or is eager to start working soon.

For eg: *This part of the old city **is set to** undergo a modern renovation.*

It makes sense in the context of the given sentence since it conveys that the Indian Railways is prepared to launch new special trains for the Ardh Kumbh Mela.

The verb form ‘setting’ in the given sentence does not convey the same meaning. Hence, the error is in **option 3.**

questions.question: Adults can hear a sound with pitch:
questions.solution:
As is mentioned clearly in the passage:

*“The device emits a **seventeen kilohertz buzz, a pitch too high for older ears** to register but, is ear-splitting for younger people.”*

According to the text, the device known as the Mosquito emits a seventeen kilohertz buzz. It is stated that this pitch is too high for older ears to register, suggesting that adults cannot hear sounds above this frequency range.

Therefore, the sound with a pitch between **15-17 kilohertz falls** within the range that adults can hear.

questions.question: The phrase ‘to ply an honest trade’ means

options.text: to carry out some kind of trade
to work without a stop at something
to travel to sell something is _________
to work steadily at one’s business

questions.solution:
The phrase **‘to ply an honest trade’** means ‘to work steadily and regularly at one’s particular kind of work’.

For eg.

*Despite the dominance of big supermarkets everywhere, our city’s local vendors **still ply their trade** as they have done for years.*

Hence, **option 1 is correct.**

questions.question: Which word indicates the tone of the author in the last paragraph?
questions.solution:
A **sarcastic **tone is marked by the speaker using irony to mock, convey contempt or humorously criticize something.

We can see from the last paragraph of the passage that while the author talks about the ring tone as a “*celebration*” and “*an ingenious guerrilla tactic in youth’s eternal war against adult authority*”, he is being humorous and not literal.

He also displays some form of contempt when he asks the rhetorical question “*What was wrong with ‘Vibrate only’?*”.-

Hence, the tone of the last paragraph is clearly **sarcastic** and the correct answer is **option 2.**

questions.question: What does The Times celebrate?

options.text: the ingenious way the youth have turned the tables on adults
youth anarchy in devising a way to disrupt classes
The end of the war between adult authority and youth anarchy

questions.solution:
As the author mentions in the passage:

*“**The Times**, in a welcome but highly uncharacteristic embrace of anarchy, **has celebrated this development **as an ingenious guerrilla tactic in **youth’s eternal war against adult authority.”***

Hence, we can see that **option 1 is correct.**

questions.question: Why does the author use these adjective ‘yobs, scamps, ne’er-do-wells, scapegraces, ruffians, tosspots and bravos’ to refer to younger people?

options.text: To laugh at youth and their behaviour
To claim that all youth are anarchic and disruptive
To indicate that adults always see youth as disruptive
To use fashionable terms to talk about youth

questions.solution:
As the author mentions in the passage:

*“...driving hooligans, yobs, scamps, ne’er-do-wells, scapegraces, ruffians, tosspots, and bravos **away from places where grownups are attempting to ply an honest trade**.”*

We can understand from the context of the given sentence that the author wants to suggest that these terms describe the way in which adults generally perceive the younger generation.

Hence, **option 3 is correct.**

questions.question: **Select the grammatically correct sentence.**

options.text: I was scared out of my wits first time I got on a plane.
I was scared out of my wits the first time I got on a plane.
I was scared out of my wits the first time I got on plane.
I was scared out of my wits a first time I got on the plane.

questions.solution:
To reach the correct answer, we must look at whether the given sentences correctly make use of articles.

The correct sentence clearly requires articles at two points:

***1. …the ****first time I got on a plane* – here, the definite article ‘the’ will be used since a **specific **incident is being referenced.

*2. …first time I got on **a **plane *– here, the indefinite article ‘a’ will be used since the noun ‘plane’ is being mentioned in the sentence for the first time.

The only sentence that follows both these conditions is **option 2. **

questions.question:
**Select the sentence that best reports the sentence given below.**

“If you do not return the books, the library will cancel your membership,” said the librarian to the boy.

options.text: The librarian warned the boy to return the books if he did not want his membership to be cancelled.
The librarian said that he would cancel the membership if the books were not returned.
The librarian told the boy to return the books or else he would cancel the membership.
The librarian warned the boy that the library would cancel his membership if he did not return the books.

questions.solution:
Here, the given sentence is in active speech and needs to be converted into reported speech.

Therefore, it needs to follow the following rules:

 
• Omit all inverted commas or quotation marks.
 
• If the verb inside the inverted commas/quotation marks is in the present tense, change it into the corresponding past tense.
 
• Change and use pronouns appropriately:
 
You >> he

 Your >> his

 

The option that fulfils all these conditions is **option 4, and is hence the correct answer.**

questions.question:
**Select the appropriate word to complete the sentence.**

He played down his _________ of becoming chairman.
questions.solution:
The word ‘**chances**’ is used to mean the possibility of something happening. It is often used with a possessive pronoun to identify the person to whom the possibility applies.

For eg*.: *

 
• *I am afraid your **chances **of winning the lottery are quite slim.*
 
• *Tara thinks her **chances **of getting a promotion this year are looking good!*

 

This fits perfectly in the context of the sentence where the possibility of someone becoming a chairman is being discussed.

‘**Luck**’ and ‘**occasion**’ do not fit meaningfully here. The word ‘**possibility**’ is rejected since unlike ‘chances’ it cannot be used with a possessive pronoun.

Hence, **option 2 is correct.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.**

COLOSSAL
questions.solution:
The word ‘**co****lossal’ **means extremely large or great.

Clearly, the word most opposite in meaning to the given word is ‘**tiny’** which means extremely small.

**Hence, option 1 is correct.**

__Note:__

 
• **Evident** means clearly seen or understood; obvious.
 
• **Immense** is a synonym of 'colossal’.

questions.question:
**Select the sentence that best expresses the active form of the sentence given below.**

He is said to be one of the finest pianists in the world.

options.text: He said he is one of the finest pianists in the world
People said him to be one of the finest pianists in the world.
People said he was one of the finest pianists in the world.
People say he is one of the finest pianists in the world.

questions.solution:
The given passive sentence does not have an object. If a passive sentence does not have a subject, then a dummy subject is used instead when converting it into an active sentence.

In this case, the most appropriate dummy subject, as understood from the context, would be ‘**people’**.

Also, the tense in both active and passive sentences should remain the same. The tense of the given sentence is simple present and hence, the passive sentence would also be in the same tense.

Hence, **option 4** is the right answer since it fulfils both these conditions.

Note: (In the official exam papers, each occurrence of the word ‘*pianists’* has been erroneously spelled as ‘*pianist’*.)

questions.question: **Select the wrongly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The incorrectly spelt word is **option 2. **It should be correctly spelt as **principally, **which means ‘chiefly or for the most part’.

Here are the meanings of all the given words:

 
• **Primarily** – for the most part; mainly
 
• **Priestly** – relating to a priest or priests
 
• **Princely** – suitable for a prince, very grand

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the idioms given in CAPITALS.**

TO BE ALL EARS

options.text: To hide and listen to something
to be unwilling to listen to something
To eagerly want to hear about something
To strain to listen to something

questions.solution:
The idiom **‘to be all ears’ **means to listen eagerly about something.

For eg.

*As soon as Nikita started telling her story, you could see that everyone **was all ears**.*

Hence, **option 3 is correct.**
